raw_segments.text: The law of the jungle, which never orders anything without a reason, forbids every beast
to eat man except when he is killing to show his children how to kill, and then he must
hunt outside the hunting grounds of his pack or tribe.
The real reason for this is that man-killing means, sooner or later, the arrival of white
men on elephants, with guns, and hundreds of brown men with gongs and rockets and torches.
Then everybody in the jungle suffers.
The reason the beasts give among themselves is that man is the weakest and most defenseless
of all living things, and it is unsportsmanlike to touch him.
They say too and it is true that man-eaters become mangy and lose their teeth.
